title: Fats Waller's band: Tom Whaley, rehearsals and the left-hand corner
summary: Thomas worked with Waller only a month or two. He describes early-morning rehearsals under Tom Whaley, Henderson's band as the greatest, and a Yale gig before Waller's Apollo date.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: No. It couldn't have been over a month. I'm almost sure. Maybe allow me two months. May I tell you about this? May I tell you this story? If I may.

Well, Fats was a tremendous musician, as you know. And, during the rehearsal he'd get the shows together and to lead the shows off, there's afellow that's a conductor there that by the name of Tom Hurley.

Yeah, Tom Whaley. We always speak of him as a fine musician. I think he's working with the Duke now. And, we saw sometimes, maybe whenever we got in town, 4 o'clock in the morning, 5 o'clock in the morning... rehearsal down near the time had for show time. MW after leaving Henderson, who I thought he was the greatest band in the world.

I thought so. I worked in it ... he had the greatest band in the world because that's the way he thought. And the way we got together, the way I got together with Smack, I had a little deal called the Left Hand Corner. That figured That's means the first note. I figured if you could interpret (Q) the first note, something must be happening for the rest of them, you know. So he appreciated my little idea and so we had pretty good style.
But, you were going to tell a story about Fats.

Fats Waller. Well, there came a day -- I think we made a gig at Yale. It was Henderson's band and Fats was working as a single, you know. He was getting ready to organize himself a group, a big band and so we were going going to

the Apollo Theater ... with Charlie Turner's band, you know. So we had a couple of gigs to get the band together. So, on our way to Atlantic City, so the first damn time I'd seen the whole band together on time because me I like to be on time. I'm slow. I get like there and all things happen.
Yeah. Trumpet chops and that kind of thing ... So we got down. I think Fats was living along somewhere at 118th Street and 7th Avenue. I'm jumping ahead of my story. (blank space on tape)
